{{Wireless adapter |brand=Ruckus Wireless |model=MPE5AC33A |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=08/09/2013 |manuf_country= |is_manuf=No |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |availability= |if=Mini PCIe (oversized) |if_bus_version= |if_connector_type= |form_factor=AP wireless module |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |id_string= |fcc_id=S9G-MPE5AC33A |ic_id=5912A-MPE5AC33A |chip1_brand=Qualcomm Atheros |chip1_model=QCA9880-2R4E;QCA9880-2R4E, N6K395.0ZC; 1248, KOREA; |chip2_brand= |chip2_model= |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |chip4_brand= |chip4_model= |addl_chips= |accessible_UART=No |flags= |ant_conn=U.FL |802dot11_protocols=an+ac |txchains=3 |rxchains=3 |sstreams=3 |oui= |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} "GD39", "5G", "RUCKUS WIRELESS", "(C)2013 Ruckus Wireless Inc.", "FAB 100-11241-001 REV 2", "ASM 120-11242-"<001 sticker>"REV"<2 sticker>" is silkscreened on the back of the card in the FCC photos.
The module is shown with what is presumably a '''QCA''' AP135 dev board. :The board has a Mini PCIe slot, two USB ports, and what appears to be a Mini PCI slot.. It is using a QCA95xx WiSoC.
The power supply included with the AP135 board in the FCC photos is a '''Ruckus Wireless''' branded MPBS-12020000 / P/N: 740-64120-011 (100-240VAC ~ 50/60Hz, 0.65A -> 12VDC, 1.5A).
